```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vanDyk_2026_atazanavir"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00592-26> (open access, PMC13436004)
* Supplement: `aac.00592-26-s0001.pdf` (Table S1, dosing by weight band;
  Figure S1, external-validation VPC). It contains no model code or extra
  parameter values.

Ritonavir-boosted atazanavir (ATV/r) is a once-daily option for
subsequent-line antiretroviral therapy in children, but rifampicin-based
tuberculosis treatment strongly induces its clearance. van Dyk et al. pooled
intensive data from the CHAPAS-4 trial with sparse data from the VirTUAL
study to build a pediatric atazanavir model, then simulated WHO weight-band
dosing with and without rifampicin, carrying adult induction factors from
the DERIVE trial (packaged here as `Kengo_2025_atazanavir`).

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("vanDyk_2026_atazanavir")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

# Population

`r rxode2::rxode(mod)$population$n_subjects` children and adolescents
(60 from CHAPAS-4 in Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe; 10 from VirTUAL in South
Africa and Uganda) contributed 518 atazanavir concentrations (van Dyk 2026
Table 1). Median (range) age was 10.9 (3.2-17.7) years and weight 29
(15-85) kg; 56% were male. All received once-daily ATV/r: 150/100 mg
(2.9%), 200/75 mg (34%) or 200/100 mg (7.1%) as separate tablets, or the
300/100 mg fixed-dose combination (FDC, 56%). NRTI backbones were
TAF/emtricitabine (49%), abacavir/lamivudine (31%), zidovudine/lamivudine
(13%) and TDF/lamivudine (7.1%).

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2-compartment, lag + sequential zero-/first-order absorption | -- | Results 'Pharmacokinetic analysis'; Methods |
| `lcl` CL/F at 27 kg | 4.8 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc` Vc/F at 27 kg | 41.2 L | Table 2 |
| `lq` Q/F at 27 kg | 0.418 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvp` Vp/F at 27 kg | 47.5 L | Table 2 |
| `ltlag` lag time | 1 h (fixed) | Table 2 and footnote g |
| `ld1` zero-order input duration D1 | 1.04 h | Table 2 |
| `lka` absorption rate constant | 2.23 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lfdepot` bioavailability | 1 (fixed) | Table 2 |
| `e_fdc0_fdepot` non-FDC change in F | -26.7% | Table 2 and footnote c; Results |
| `e_rif_qd_cl` CL change, rifampicin + once-daily ATV/r | 3.12-fold (fixed) | Table 2 footnote d; Methods 'Simulations' |
| `e_rif_bid_cl` CL change, rifampicin + twice-daily ATV/r | 2.04-fold (fixed) | Table 2 footnote d; Methods 'Simulations' |
| `e_rif_qd_fdepot` F change, rifampicin + once-daily ATV/r | -53% (fixed) | Table 2 footnote d; Methods 'Simulations' |
| `e_selfadmin_iov` BOV-on-F scaling after an unobserved dose | 1.43 (fixed) | Table 2; Results |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` allometric exponents, 27 kg reference | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Methods; Table 2 footnote a |
| `etalcl` BSV CL | 18.9% CV -> omega^2 0.0351 | Table 2, footnote f |
| `etaiov_tlag_*` BOV lag | 60.5% CV (fixed) -> 0.312 | Table 2, footnotes f, g |
| `etaiov_d1_*` BOV D1 | 111% CV -> 0.803 | Table 2, footnote f |
| `etaiov_ka_*` BOV ka | 162% CV -> 1.288 | Table 2, footnote f |
| `etaiov_fdepot_*` BOV F | 34.7% CV -> 0.114 | Table 2, footnote f |
| `propSd` proportional error | 11.8% | Table 2 |
| `addSdChapas4`, `addSdVirtual` additive error | 0.021, 0.006 mg/L (fixed) | Table 2 footnote e (20% of LLOQ 0.105 / 0.030 mg/L) |

The variances are `log((CV/100)^2 + 1)` because Table 2 footnote f defines
the reported %CV as `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1) * 100`.

# Virtual cohort

The paper's simulation (Methods 'Simulations', Figure 2) populates four
weight bands with uniformly distributed weights and doses them by the
CHAPAS-4 scheme: 200 mg atazanavir below 25 kg, 300 mg at 25 kg and above,
each given once daily without rifampicin, once daily with rifampicin, or
twice daily with rifampicin. 200 virtual children are drawn per band and
scenario (the paper used 1,000 per band).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260717)
n_per_arm <- 200
bands <- tibble::tibble(
  band = factor(c("15-19.9 kg", "20-24.9 kg", "25-34.9 kg", "35-44.9 kg"),
                levels = c("15-19.9 kg", "20-24.9 kg", "25-34.9 kg", "35-44.9 kg")),
  wt_lo = c(15, 20, 25, 35),
  wt_hi = c(19.9, 24.9, 34.9, 44.9),
  dose = c(200, 200, 300, 300)
)
scenarios <- tibble::tibble(
  scenario = factor(c("ATV/r OD", "ATV/r OD + RIF", "ATV/r BD + RIF"),
                    levels = c("ATV/r OD", "ATV/r OD + RIF", "ATV/r BD + RIF")),
  CONMED_RIF = c(0, 1, 1),
  REGI_BID = c(0, 0, 1),
  ii = c(24, 24, 12)
)

cohort <- tidyr::expand_grid(bands, scenarios, rep = seq_len(n_per_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT = stats::runif(dplyr::n(), wt_lo, wt_hi)
  )

cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(band) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), median_wt = median(WT), min_wt = min(WT),
                   max_wt = max(WT), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated weights by band (all three scenarios pooled).")
```

# Simulation

Doses are given for 28 days to reach steady state (the slow peripheral
exchange gives a terminal half-life near 90 h) and the final 24 h are
sampled. Each dose record uses `rate = -2`, so rxode2 applies the model's
modelled zero-order duration D1 after the absorption lag. All doses share
occasion 1 (`OCC = 1`), so the between-occasion deviations act as
subject-level variability in this steady-state exercise, and every dose is
treated as observed (`SELFADMIN = 0`).

```{r sim-fn}
make_events <- function(cohort, form_fdc, days = 28) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    dplyr::rowwise() |>
    dplyr::reframe(id = id, time = seq(0, days * 24 - ii, by = ii), amt = dose) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = -2)
  t_end <- days * 24
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(t_end - 24, t_end, by = 0.5), t_end - 24 + c(1, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5))))
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
  covs <- cohort |>
    dplyr::select(id, WT, CONMED_RIF, REGI_BID) |>
    dplyr::mutate(FORM_FDC = form_fdc, OCC = 1, SELFADMIN = 0, STUDY_VIRTUAL = 0)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(covs, by = "id")
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260717)
ev_fdc <- make_events(cohort, form_fdc = 1)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_fdc, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, band, scenario, dose), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - (28 * 24 - 24))
```

## Structural check: steady-state AUC equals F x dose / CL

With the random effects removed, the AUC over the last 24 h of a 28-day run
must equal the daily bioavailable dose divided by clearance. This checks the
dose route, the allometric reference, the formulation factor and both
rifampicin branches against Table 2 in closed form, independent of any seed.

```{r closed-form}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_cohort <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  tibble::tibble(WT = c(17.5, 27, 40)),
  scenarios,
  FORM_FDC = c(0, 1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), dose = ifelse(WT < 25, 200, 300))

ev_typ <- typ_cohort |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(id = id, time = seq(0, 28 * 24 - ii, by = ii), amt = dose) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = -2) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = typ_cohort$id, time = seq(27 * 24, 28 * 24, by = 0.05)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(typ_cohort, id, WT, CONMED_RIF, REGI_BID, FORM_FDC) |>
      dplyr::mutate(OCC = 1, SELFADMIN = 0, STUDY_VIRTUAL = 0),
    by = "id"
  )

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame",
                           atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10)

auc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(typ_cohort, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    f = (1 - 0.267 * (1 - FORM_FDC)) * (1 - 0.53 * CONMED_RIF * (1 - REGI_BID)),
    cl = 4.8 * (WT / 27)^0.75 *
      ifelse(CONMED_RIF == 1, ifelse(REGI_BID == 1, 2.04, 3.12), 1),
    auc_expected = f * dose * (24 / ii) / cl,
    pct_diff = 100 * (auc - auc_expected) / auc_expected
  )

auc_typ |>
  dplyr::select(WT, scenario, FORM_FDC, dose, auc, auc_expected, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename("Weight (kg)" = WT, "Scenario" = scenario, "FDC" = FORM_FDC,
                "Dose (mg)" = dose, "AUC0-24 solved" = auc,
                "F x daily dose / CL" = auc_expected, "% diff" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value steady-state AUC0-24 (mg*h/L) against the closed form.")

# Both sides use the same typical parameters, so the difference is numerical
# (trapezoid on a 0.05 h grid and residual approach to steady state).
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_typ$pct_diff) < 1))
```

## Replicate Figure 2

Replicates Figure 2 of van Dyk 2026 (simulated steady-state Ctrough and
AUC0-24 by weight band and scenario).

```{r fig2-data}
exposure <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(tad >= 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, band, scenario, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc24 = sum(diff(tad) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    ctrough = Cc[which.max(tad)],
    cmin = min(Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 5}
exposure |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(ctrough, auc24), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("ctrough", "auc24"),
                                labels = c("Ctrough (mg/L)", "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(scenario, value, fill = band)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = function(y) {
      q <- stats::quantile(y, c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95))
      data.frame(ymin = q[1], lower = q[2], middle = q[3], upper = q[4], ymax = q[5])
    },
    geom = "boxplot", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(metric = factor("Ctrough (mg/L)", levels = c("Ctrough (mg/L)", "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)")),
                               y = c(0.15, 0.014)),
             aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed", colour = c("blue", "red")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Treatment regimen", y = NULL, fill = "Weight band",
       caption = "Boxes: 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentiles. Dashed: MEC 0.15 mg/L (blue), PA-IC90 0.014 mg/L (red).") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The paper's Results report the share of simulated troughs above the
protein-adjusted IC90 (PA-IC90, 0.014 mg/L) and the minimum effective
concentration (MEC, 0.15 mg/L):

```{r target-attainment}
attain <- exposure |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    above_pa_ic90 = 100 * mean(ctrough > 0.014),
    above_mec = 100 * mean(ctrough > 0.15),
    above_pa_ic90_cmin = 100 * mean(cmin > 0.014),
    above_mec_cmin = 100 * mean(cmin > 0.15),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    paper = c("100% / 97.4%", "over 75% below PA-IC90 / 0% above MEC", "100% / 98.6%")
  )

attain |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario" = scenario,
                "% Ctrough > PA-IC90" = above_pa_ic90,
                "% Ctrough > MEC" = above_mec,
                "% Cmin > PA-IC90" = above_pa_ic90_cmin,
                "% Cmin > MEC" = above_mec_cmin,
                "Paper (> PA-IC90 / > MEC)" = paper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Margins are wide: each scenario sits far from the threshold being tested,
# so these do not depend on which subjects land in the tails.
oc <- attain$scenario
stopifnot(
  attain$above_mec[oc == "ATV/r OD"] > 90,
  attain$above_mec[oc == "ATV/r OD + RIF"] < 5,
  attain$above_pa_ic90[oc == "ATV/r OD + RIF"] < 50,
  attain$above_mec[oc == "ATV/r BD + RIF"] > 90,
  attain$above_mec_cmin[oc == "ATV/r OD"] > 90,
  attain$above_pa_ic90_cmin[oc == "ATV/r OD + RIF"] < 50
)
```

Ctrough here is the concentration at the end of the dosing interval, just
before the next dose. Because each dose is held back by the 1 h lag and then
enters over D1, concentrations keep falling briefly after the next dose, so
the interval minimum (Cmin) is a little lower than Ctrough; the paper does
not say which it plotted. Without rifampicin and with twice-daily ATV/r plus
rifampicin, the simulated attainment matches the paper. With once-daily
ATV/r plus rifampicin, the simulated troughs are about 0.01 mg/L, on the
steep part of the attainment curve around the PA-IC90. About two thirds of
simulated children fall below it, where the paper reports over three
quarters. Both definitions give a similar share, so the trough definition
does not explain the difference.

## Replicate Figure 1 (CHAPAS-4 visual predictive check)

Replicates the left panel of Figure 1 of van Dyk 2026 in outline: a
CHAPAS-4-like cohort (weight-band shares from Table 1) sampled at steady
state at the trial's week-6 times. Children under 25 kg take 200 mg as
separate tablets (`FORM_FDC = 0`); heavier children take the 300/100 mg FDC.
The home doses before the PK day are unobserved (`SELFADMIN = 1`, occasion 1)
and the supervised PK-day dose is occasion 2.

```{r vpc}
set.seed(4)
n_vpc <- 200
vpc_cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_vpc),
  band = sample(1:4, n_vpc, replace = TRUE, prob = c(12, 16, 18, 14))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    WT = stats::runif(n_vpc, c(15, 20, 25, 35)[band], c(19.9, 24.9, 34.9, 64)[band]),
    dose = ifelse(WT < 25, 200, 300),
    FORM_FDC = as.numeric(WT >= 25)
  )
pk_day <- 27 * 24
vpc_doses <- vpc_cohort |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(id = id, time = seq(0, pk_day, by = 24), amt = dose) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = -2,
                OCC = ifelse(time < pk_day, 1, 2),
                SELFADMIN = ifelse(time < pk_day, 1, 0))
vpc_obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = vpc_cohort$id,
                              tad = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = pk_day + tad, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
                OCC = ifelse(tad == 0, 1, 2), SELFADMIN = ifelse(tad == 0, 1, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(-tad)
vpc_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(vpc_doses, vpc_obs) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(vpc_cohort, id, WT, FORM_FDC), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(CONMED_RIF = 0, REGI_BID = 0, STUDY_VIRTUAL = 0)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(4)
vpc_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, vpc_ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= pk_day) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - pk_day)

vpc_q <- vpc_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
                   .groups = "drop")

ggplot(vpc_q, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Atazanavir (mg/L)",
       caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval of simulated observations (with residual error).") +
  theme_bw()
```

Read off the published Figure 1 (left), the observed median is about
4.5 mg/L at 4 h and about 0.5 mg/L at 24 h.

```{r vpc-check}
vpc_tab <- vpc_q |>
  dplyr::filter(tad %in% c(4, 24)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fig1_median = c(4.5, 0.5),
                ratio = p50 / fig1_median)
vpc_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Time after dose (h)" = tad, "Sim 5th" = p05, "Sim median" = p50,
                "Sim 95th" = p95, "Figure 1 observed median (read off)" = fig1_median,
                "Ratio" = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# The Figure 1 medians are read off a log axis, so the tolerance is broad;
# a misplaced allometric reference or dose route moves these by far more.
stopifnot(all(vpc_tab$ratio > 0.6 & vpc_tab$ratio < 1.6))
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over the final 24 h of each simulated child, grouped by
scenario and weight band.

```{r pknca}
conc_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), tad >= 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = paste(scenario, band, sep = " | ")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, group, scenario, band, tad, Cc)
dose_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, scenario, band, dose) |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = paste(scenario, band, sep = " | "), tad = 0)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ tad | group + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, dose ~ tad | group + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE,
                        tmax = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "ctrough", "cmin", "cmax", "tmax"))

nca_df |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario | band" = group, "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast,
                "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Ctrough (mg/L)" = ctrough,
                "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin, "Tmax (h)" = tmax) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Median steady-state NCA (200 simulated children per group).")
```

## Comparison with Figure 2

The paper reports its simulated exposures only graphically. The medians
below were read off Figure 2 by the maintainers (log axes, so roughly
+/-10% precision). The Figure 2 trough medians are placed beside both the
end-of-interval Ctrough and the interval Cmin.

```{r compare}
fig2_ref <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  scenario = c("ATV/r OD", "ATV/r OD + RIF", "ATV/r BD + RIF"),
  band = c("15-19.9 kg", "20-24.9 kg", "25-34.9 kg", "35-44.9 kg")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    group = paste(scenario, band, sep = " | "),
    auclast = c(60, 50, 60, 46, 8.5, 7.5, 8.5, 7.3, 60, 48, 58, 46),
    ctrough = c(0.50, 0.49, 0.65, 0.53, 0.0085, 0.0070, 0.0090, 0.0078,
                0.67, 0.62, 0.82, 0.75),
    cmin = ctrough
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(group, auclast, ctrough, cmin)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_df |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "ctrough", "cmin")),
  fig2_ref,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", ctrough = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, digits = 3)
if (!is.null(attr(cmp, "footnote"))) cat(attr(cmp, "footnote"))

auc_cmp <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig2_ref, by = "group") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim - auclast) / auclast)

# Centre and envelope, never a per-group extreme: a mis-scaled clearance or
# a wrong formulation reading moves every group by 25% or more.
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_cmp) == 12,
  abs(median(auc_cmp$pct)) < 10,
  max(abs(auc_cmp$pct)) < 25
)
```

The simulated AUC0-24 matches Figure 2 in every band only when every child is
given the FDC bioavailability (`FORM_FDC = 1`), which is how the simulation
above was run. With the separate-tablet bioavailability applied to the two
lower bands, as in the CHAPAS-4 dosing (Table S1), their AUC and Ctrough
would be 26.7% lower, which would not match the figure:

```{r form-reading}
auc_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(WT == 17.5) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, FORM_FDC, auc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = FORM_FDC, values_from = auc, names_prefix = "FDC_") |>
  dplyr::mutate(fig2 = c(60, 8.5, 60)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario" = scenario, "Separate tablets (FORM_FDC = 0)" = FDC_0,
                "FDC (FORM_FDC = 1)" = FDC_1, "Figure 2 median, 15-19.9 kg" = fig2) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical AUC0-24 (mg*h/L) at 17.5 kg, 200 mg, by formulation reading.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Number of occasions.** The paper treats each dose as a separate occasion
  but does not say how many occasions the data held. Six occasion slots
  (`OCC` 1-6) are carried, enough for the VirTUAL design (three visits, each
  with a home dose and a clinic dose). Doses with `OCC` outside 1-6 get no
  between-occasion deviation.
* **Unobserved-dose scaling.** Table 2 gives a 1.43-fold "scaling factor on
  BOV for the unobserved dose" and the Results say it inflates the
  between-occasion variability on bioavailability. It is applied here as a
  multiplier on the bioavailability occasion eta (standard-deviation scale),
  the form the same group's control streams use (`Kengo_2025_atazanavir`,
  `Ndzamba_2025_ethambutol`). Unlike Kengo 2025, only the bioavailability
  eta is scaled, as the paper states.
* **Rifampicin effects are assumptions, not estimates.** No atazanavir data
  were collected with rifampicin. The fixed factors (CL x3.12 and F -53%
  once daily; CL x2.04 twice daily) are the paper's adult-derived simulation
  inputs, attributed to the Kengo et al. DERIVE model. They differ slightly
  from the final estimates printed in Kengo 2025 Table 2 (3.05, 2.03 and
  -52.5%; `Kengo_2025_atazanavir`); van Dyk 2026's own values are used here.
  The rifampicin effect on ka in Kengo 2025 was not carried into this
  paper's simulations and is not part of this model.
* **Additive error by study.** The additive error was fixed to 20% of each
  laboratory's LLOQ, which differs between CHAPAS-4 (0.105 mg/L) and VirTUAL
  (0.030 mg/L); `STUDY_VIRTUAL` selects between them. It does not affect
  typical-value or individual predictions.
* **Formulation in the Figure 2 simulations.** The paper's Figure 2 medians
  are reproduced only when all bands use the FDC bioavailability; the paper
  does not say which formulation the simulations assumed. The model keeps
  the estimated separate-tablet effect, so choose `FORM_FDC` to match the
  regimen being simulated.
* **Troughs with once-daily ATV/r plus rifampicin.** The simulated median
  troughs in this scenario are 12-47% above the values read off Figure 2,
  and about two thirds of simulated children fall below the PA-IC90 where
  the paper reports over three quarters. AUC0-24 in the same scenario
  matches Figure 2 within 8%, and troughs in the other two scenarios match
  within about 20%. These troughs are around 0.01 mg/L on a log axis, where
  reading values off the figure is least precise. The paper also does not
  say whether its trough is the end-of-interval concentration or the
  interval minimum (both are reported above), nor how between-occasion
  variability was handled in its steady-state simulations. No parameter was
  adjusted. The AUC comparison, which does not depend on these choices,
  carries the assertion.
* **Figure 2 and Figure 1 reference values** were read off the published
  figures by the maintainers; the paper prints no exposure table. The adult
  reference geometric mean AUC0-24 shown as a dashed line in Figure 2
  (about 40 mg*h/L, from the paper's reference 21) is not used as a check.
* **Data-handling methods not part of the model.** M7+ handling of BLQ
  samples, exclusion of non-adherent participants and the B2 initialisation
  of one CHAPAS-4 participant are estimation-time data handling and have no
  counterpart in a simulation model.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (age, fat-free mass, ritonavir
  AUC0-24 and dose, NRTI backbone) are listed in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found for this article
  (checked 2026-11-16).
